knobs.code_doc: Layout version of the file; written automatically.

If set (< the loaded image size), the pipeline CENTER-CROPS the loaded image/noise to this size for ALL normal modelling (stages 1/2/3, sampling). The full loaded image is retained ONLY for the lens-light refit (LensLightRefitConfig), which fits the parametric lens light on the larger frame for better outer-profile / sky constraints; its cutout-invariant parameters transfer back to the cropped model unchanged. None = use the loaded image at its native size everywhere.
knobs.curated_html:
If set (and smaller than the loaded image), the pipeline center-crops the loaded image and noise map to this many pixels per side for every normal modelling stage and sampling. A full-frame data.likelihood_mask_path is center-cropped with the same offset; an already cutout-sized likelihood mask is accepted unchanged.

The full loaded frame is retained for the lens-light refit, which fits the parametric light on the larger frame for better outer-profile and sky constraints. Its cutout-invariant parameters transfer back to the cropped model unchanged, and its separate mask must match the full frame.

knobs.code_doc: Radius (arcsec) within which the lens-galaxy centre is refined from the seed position. Shrink for asymmetric lenses where a bright point-source image lies within the default 0.5" of the seed (otherwise the refinement locks onto the PS image instead of the lens galaxy).
knobs.curated_html: Radius within which the lens-galaxy centre is refined from the seed position. Shrink it for asymmetric systems where a bright point-source image lies within the search radius — otherwise the refinement locks onto the quasar image instead of the galaxy.

knobs.code_doc: Optional path to a boolean mask file (``.npy`` or ``.fits``). When provided, only ``True`` pixels contribute to the likelihood.
knobs.curated_html:
Optional boolean mask for the main lens-model likelihood — companions, diffraction spikes, cosmic-ray residuals, and detector defects. Only True pixels contribute; null disables the mask.

The .npy or .fits array may match either the modelling cutout or the original full science frame. When data.cutout_size is active and a full-frame mask is supplied, ALPACA center-crops it with exactly the same offset as the image and noise map. A cutout-sized mask is used directly.

This mask belongs to the main fit and is distinct from the full-frame light.lens.refit.mask_path. The same full-frame file may be used for both paths only when its pixel selection is intentionally suitable for both fits.
warnings: A line-of-sight perturber's LIGHT is modelled only when its catalog entry has a lens_light block — mask every other perturber galaxy here or its flux is fitted by the lens light / source and biases the fit.

knobs.code_doc: Detector pixel scale in arcsec/pixel.
knobs.curated_html: Detector pixel scale of the science image. Read it from your FITS header (CD1_1/CD2_2 or D001SCAL). Common values: drizzled HST/WFC3 = 0.04, JWST/NIRCam short-wave = 0.031. Everything angular in the pipeline (masks, priors on offsets, PS separation) is expressed in arcsec and converted with this scale, so an incorrect value silently corrupts the whole geometry.

knobs.code_doc: Radius (arcsec) of the central mask around the lens centre that is excluded from point-source detection. Shrink this when one of the images sits close to the lens galaxy.
knobs.curated_html: Radius of the central mask around the lens-galaxy centre that is excluded from point-source detection, so the bright lens core is not picked up as a fifth image. Shrink it when a genuine quasar image sits close to the lens galaxy (small-separation quads, fold configurations).

knobs.code_doc: Minimum fraction of the brightest unmasked peak for a local maximum to be accepted as a point-source candidate. Lower this for high-magnification-ratio quads where the faintest image is much dimmer than the brightest.
knobs.curated_html: Minimum fraction of the brightest unmasked peak for a local maximum to count as a point-source candidate. Lower it (e.g. to 0.05) for high-magnification-ratio quads where the faintest image is far dimmer than the brightest; raising it suppresses spurious detections from bright arc knots.

knobs.code_doc: Minimum separation (arcsec) between detected point-source images. ``None`` (default) resolves to ``2 x pix_scale`` so it tracks the detector sampling automatically.
knobs.curated_html: Minimum separation between detected point-source images. Local maxima closer than this get merged into one candidate. Two native pixels is a safe default; raise it if noise spikes near an image split one quasar image into two detections.

knobs.code_doc: Source-plane supersampling factor for the forward model. The source grid is ``source_oversample`` times finer than the data pixels and downsampled on output. Memory scales ~quadratically. Note: the supersampling factor of the INPUT PSF lives in ``psf.input.oversample`` (it describes the provided PSF file, not the observation).
knobs.curated_html: Source-plane supersampling factor of the forward model: the internal source grid is this many times finer than the data pixels and is downsampled on output. Memory scales roughly quadratically. 3 is usually plenty; 5 adds marginal accuracy at ~2.8× the memory.

knobs.code_doc: Share one centre between the Sérsic components.
Share one ellipticity between the Sérsic components.
knobs.curated_html: Couple the ellipticities of all Sersic lens-light components: L2/L3 share e1/e2 with L1. Removes four latents from a triple-Sersic model and prevents the components from twisting against each other — recommended when the extra Sersics are meant as radial-profile freedom, not isophote-twist freedom.

knobs.code_doc: Upper bound on the lens-light ellipticity components.
Lens-light model of the GD stage 1 (e.g. 'sersic', 'double-sersic', 'triple-sersic', 'MGE+double-sersic').
knobs.curated_html:
Preferred single-string interface for the lens-light model (2026-07). It sets the four legacy booleans (use_double_sersic_lens, use_triple_sersic_lens, use_mge_lens_light, mge_as_correction) consistently:

  • "sersic" — single Sersic profile.
  • "double-sersic" — bulge + envelope.
  • "triple-sersic" — plus a third component for core corrections.
  • "MGE" — a Multi-Gaussian Expansion replaces the Sersics entirely.
  • "MGE+double-sersic" / "MGE+triple-sersic" — Sersics carry bulge+envelope, a small Gaussian stack absorbs residual core mottling.

When null, the string is derived from the legacy booleans, which remain supported for old configs and are kept in sync at validation. The number of MGE components stays a separate knob (mge_n_components).

knobs.code_doc: Number of Gaussians in the MGE lens-light model.
knobs.curated_html: Number of Gaussian components in the MGE stack, log-spaced in width between mge_sigma_min and mge_sigma_max. More components give smoother radial-profile freedom at the cost of one amplitude latent each.

knobs.code_doc: Largest MGE width (arcsec).
knobs.curated_html: Width of the widest MGE Gaussian. In correction mode keep this small (a few tenths of an arcsec) so the stack stays a core correction; in full-MGE mode it must reach the lens-light envelope scale.

knobs.code_doc: Smallest MGE width (arcsec).
knobs.curated_html: Width of the narrowest MGE Gaussian. Values well below the PSF width buy nothing — the convolution washes them out.

knobs.code_doc: Optimization budget of the light-only fit.
knobs.curated_html: Optimization budget of the light-only fit.

knobs.code_doc: Build a REFIT-ONLY arc annulus (arcsec, centred on the point-source centroid = the Einstein-ring centre) instead of reusing the CF arc mask. Strongly recommended whenever ``mask_arc`` or ``ps_sigma_clip_within="arc"`` is used: the CF mask is sized for SOURCE reconstruction and is far too wide for a light fit — a typical is a 0.7-2.8" annulus, and removing it costs 1.264 -> 1.879 in GD chi2 because it deletes the whole band where the Sersic R_e lives, leaving the profile there as bare interpolation. A narrow annulus bracketing the ring removes the arc flux without that damage.

A narrow annulus bracketing the ring removes the arc flux without that damage.
Width (arcsec) of the Gaussian prior on the per-component centre offsets of the refit light (lopsidedness). Only used when `uncouple_centers` is true. Default 0.05″.

Seed the Sersic indices distinctly (2.5/1/4) instead of all at 3.0. None = follow smooth_bounds. Split out so the bijection and the init can be attributed separately — bundling them made the 2026-08-04 regression (0.837 -> 1.003 on the MGE flagship) unattributable.
: Prior half-width for the refit ellipticities (e1/e2 bounded : independently). None -> inherit model.lens_light_ellipticity_max.
Gaussian prior width on the per-component ellipticity DELTAS (twist amplitude); only used when uncouple_ellipticities is True.
knobs.curated_html: Gaussian prior width on the per-component ellipticity DELTAS (the twist amplitude); only used when uncouple_ellipticities is on.

Master switch for the staged lens-light refit. When enabled, after the cf_warmstart stage the pipeline subtracts the current (source + point-source) model from the data and fits the lens light ALONE on the residual — no mass model involved — then carries that light into cf_joint (fixed or free per stages.cf_joint.lens_light). The sampling stage frees the light again, warm-started from the refit values.

knobs.code_doc: If True (default), perturbers IN FRONT of the lens plane are frozen at their stage-2 values during stage 3 while the refit light is frozen. Foreground masses deflect the grid the main-plane light is evaluated on; letting them move drags the frozen galaxy render sub-pixel across the cusp and prints a core dipole. With a frozen light, nothing else that sets its frame may move.

Zero-weight the CF ARC MASK region during the light-only fit. The refit target ``data - (source+PS)`` still carries the arc when ``simple_source="stage1"`` (the smooth stage-1 source cannot reproduce arc detail), and that leftover flux is real signal the parametric light must not chase. Excluding it POSITIONALLY removes it without the one-sided selection bias a residual clip introduces — membership is decided by geometry, not by how far the data sits above the current model. Requires an active ``model.corr_field.arc_mask``.
knobs.curated_html:
Zero-weight the arc region during the light-only fit. The refit target data − (source+PS) still carries arc flux when simple_source="stage1" (a smooth stage-1 source cannot reproduce arc detail), and that leftover is real signal the parametric light must not chase. Excluding it positionally removes it without the one-sided selection bias a residual clip introduces — membership is decided by geometry, not by how far the data sits above the current model.

arc_mask_inner_radius/arc_mask_outer_radius (float | null) build a REFIT-ONLY annulus (arcsec, centred on the point-source centroid) instead of reusing the CF arc mask — strongly recommended: the CF mask is sized for source reconstruction and is far too wide for a light fit; removing that whole band deletes exactly where the Sersic effective radius lives. A narrow annulus bracketing the ring removes the arc flux without that damage.

knobs.code_doc: Bigger-cutout refit: when DataConfig.cutout_size crops the modelling image, the refit runs on the FULL loaded frame instead. mask_path is the likelihood mask for THAT larger frame (masks field galaxies outside the lens; keeps lens+sky active). Its shape must match the full loaded image, not the cropped model. Required when the full frame is larger than the modelling cutout.
knobs.curated_html:
Mask for the lens-light refit only. When data.cutout_size crops the modelling image, the refit deliberately runs on the full loaded frame so the galaxy's faint wings and sky remain constrained. This mask must therefore match the full frame—not the modelling cutout—and should exclude field galaxies while keeping the lens and sky active.

Unlike a full-frame data.likelihood_mask_path, this mask is not center-cropped. The same full-frame file can be assigned to both settings only when the desired pixel selection is genuinely identical.

knobs.code_doc: MGE components for the refit (None = model.mge_n_components).
knobs.curated_html: MGE components for the refit light model; null inherits light.lens.mge.n_components.

knobs.code_doc: Upper bound of the Sérsic index n of every refit component (default 8). Pairs with `n_sersic_min`; a component at either bound is a warning sign (guide §9.3).

Sersic-index bounds for the refit. Default floor 0.2 (measured: the data can want a near-Gaussian core; a 0.5 floor blocks it and prints an over-bright annulus around the core). n = 0.5 is a GAUSSIAN, and a triple-sersic refit can drive a component onto it from above even with smooth bounds — i.e. the fit wants a Gaussian core component and the floor is what stops it. Lowering it is the one evidence-backed knob, but there is little room: herculens approximates b_n = 1.9992*n - 0.3271, which reaches ZERO at n = 0.164, below which the profile degenerates to flat. Below ~0.35 treat the profile as a fitting basis, not a Sersic.
knobs.curated_html: Sersic-index floor for the refit (n_sersic_max = 8.0 is the ceiling). The worked example uses 0.2, allowing a triple-Sersic refit to use a very shallow core component. There is little room below it: the Sersic normalisation approximation reaches zero at n ≈ 0.164, below which the profile degenerates to flat. Below ~0.35, treat the profile as a flexible fitting basis rather than a conventional Sersic component.

knobs.code_doc: Complexity of the refit light model. "same" = the main model's ``lens_light``; otherwise any lens_light option ("sersic", "double-sersic", "triple-sersic", "MGE", "MGE+double-sersic", "MGE+triple-sersic") — it may be MORE complex than the first try. From the refit onward this becomes the lens-light parametrization.
knobs.curated_html: Complexity of the refit light model. "same" reuses light.lens.initial; any other lens-light option ("sersic", "double-sersic", "triple-sersic", "MGE", "MGE+double-sersic", "MGE+triple-sersic") may be MORE complex than the first try. From the refit onward this becomes the lens-light parametrization of the whole pipeline. The shipped example uses "triple-sersic". (This key was previously spelled lens_light; the old spelling is still accepted on input.)

knobs.code_doc: Radius (arcsec) of the region around each point source that is downweighted or masked. Used by ``"downweight"``/``"mask"`` only; under ``"sigma_clip"`` the region is still computed, but purely as a diagnostic overlay (it carries zero weight in the fit).
knobs.curated_html: Radius of the region around each point source that is downweighted or masked. Used by "downweight"/"mask"; under "sigma_clip" the region is still computed but only as a diagnostic overlay (zero weight in the fit).

knobs.code_doc: DEPRECATED alias kept for old configs: ``True`` means ``ps_treatment="mask"``. Ignored when ``ps_treatment`` is set explicitly.

Clip threshold in sigma for ``ps_treatment="sigma_clip"``; ``None`` resolves to the 4.0 default. Ignored in the other modes. Setting it without a ``ps_treatment`` selects ``"sigma_clip"`` (the pre-2026-08 "clip alone" idiom, ``ps_mask=false`` + ``ps_downweight_radius=0``).
knobs.curated_html: Clip threshold in sigma for ps_treatment="sigma_clip"; null resolves to 4.0 whenever clipping is active. Ignored in the other modes.

knobs.code_doc: Binary-dilate the clipped set by this many pixels (default 1). A bare threshold clips the PSF CORE but leaves the wings just below it, and those wings are exactly the flux the Sersic would otherwise absorb; one ring of growth removes them. 0 disables the growth.
Max sigma-clip reweight passes (default 3); stops early once the clipped-pixel set stops changing.
knobs.curated_html: Maximum sigma-clip reweight passes; stops early once the clipped-pixel set stops changing. Related fine-tuning: ps_sigma_clip_grow (int, default 1) binary-dilates the clipped set — a bare threshold clips the PSF core but leaves the wings just below it, and one ring of growth removes exactly the flux the Sersic would otherwise absorb; ps_sigma_clip_within ("all" | "arc" | "ps_aperture", default "all") confines where the clip may reject — an unrestricted clip also deletes lens-light pixels wherever the parametric profile fits badly (typically the galaxy core), which is the opposite of its purpose.

knobs.code_doc: Where the residual clip may reject: ``"all"`` (default), ``"arc"`` (only inside the arc mask) or ``"ps_aperture"``. An unrestricted clip also deletes lens-light pixels wherever the parametric profile fits badly — typically the galaxy CORE — which is the opposite of its purpose; confining it keeps the light intact.

How the light-only fit protects itself from point-source residuals. The three modes are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — this is the single knob: - ``"downweight"`` (default): inflate sigma 100x inside ``ps_downweight_radius`` of each point source. - ``"mask"``: zero-weight that same region entirely. - ``"sigma_clip"``: no positional PS region at all. Fit once over the whole frame, then reject pixels by RESIDUAL — anything with ``|target - light| / sigma > ps_sigma_clip`` is zero-weighted and the light is refit, iterating until the clipped set is stable. Rejects PS cores, cosmic rays and neighbour-galaxy wings wherever they actually land instead of trusting a fixed radius, and keeps every good pixel a positional mask would have thrown away (the PS aperture covers a large part of the galaxy's own core). Whichever mode is used, it is internal to the refit only — the likelihood mask used by the main pipeline is untouched.
knobs.curated_html:
How the light-only fit protects itself from point-source residuals — the three modes are mutually exclusive and this is the single knob:

  • "downweight" — inflate sigma 100× inside ps_downweight_radius of each point source.
  • "mask" — zero-weight that same region entirely.
  • "sigma_clip" — no positional region at all: fit over the whole frame, then reject pixels by RESIDUAL (|target − light|/sigma > ps_sigma_clip) and refit, iterating until the clipped set is stable. Rejects PS cores, cosmic rays and neighbour-galaxy wings wherever they actually land, and keeps every good pixel a positional mask would have thrown away.

Whichever mode is used, it is internal to the refit only — the main pipeline's likelihood mask is untouched.

knobs.code_doc: Source used for the (source+PS) subtraction the lens light is refit on. "cf" (default): the stage-2 correlated-field source — but a noisy CF source leaks flux to the cutout edges and contaminates the refit target. "stage1": use the SMOOTH stage-1 shapelets source instead, so the refit target is clean; the CF source then fits the residual arc detail in stage 3 with the light frozen. Decouples the light refit from CF noise.
knobs.curated_html: Which source model is subtracted (with the point sources) to build the refit target. "cf": the cf_warmstart correlated-field source — but a noisy CF source leaks flux to the cutout edges and contaminates the target. "stage1": the SMOOTH stage-1 shapelets source, so the target is clean; the CF source then fits the residual arc detail in cf_joint with the light frozen. Decouples the light refit from CF noise.

knobs.code_doc: If set (MJy/sr), the UNIFORM sky is FIXED to this value during the refit (e.g. an externally calculated sky level).
knobs.curated_html: If set (surface-brightness units of the image), the UNIFORM sky component is FIXED to this value during the refit — e.g. an externally calibrated sky level.

knobs.code_doc: Bound the Sersic index and ellipticities with BIJECTIONS (n = 0.5 + 7.5*sigmoid, e = 0.4*tanh) instead of ``jnp.clip``. Default False. A hard clip has ZERO gradient outside its bounds, so a parameter Adam pushes past one is dead and can never return — not a constraint but a trap, and the direct cause of triple-Sersic refits landing on ``n_sersic = 0.500`` exactly with unphysical companions. Also seeds the Sersic indices distinctly (2.5/1/4, matched to the R_e seeds) rather than all at 3.0, which is a symmetric start the components readily collapse out of. Set False to reproduce runs made before 2026-08-04 bit-for-bit.
knobs.curated_html: Bound the Sersic index and ellipticities with BIJECTIONS (n = 0.5 + 7.5·sigmoid, e = 0.4·tanh) instead of a hard clip, and seed the Sersic indices distinctly (2.5/1/4) rather than all at 3.0. A hard clip has zero gradient outside its bounds, so a parameter Adam pushes past one is dead and can never return — a trap, not a constraint. Measured on real data the trap removal did not improve the fits (the data genuinely wants the n = 0.5 boundary), so the default is off; keep it available for diagnosing future parameter railing. distinct_n_init (bool | null, default follows this flag) splits the seeding choice out so bijection and init can be attributed separately.

knobs.code_doc: Per-component CENTER deltas (lopsidedness); analogous to the twist.
knobs.curated_html: Per-component centre deltas (lopsidedness) — the positional analogue of the ellipticity twist. center_shift_sigma (float, default 0.05) is the Gaussian prior width on the deltas. Two further stability switches share this block: freeze_foreground_perts (bool, default true) freezes foreground-plane perturbers at their warmstart values while the refit light is frozen in cf_joint — foreground masses deflect the grid the light is evaluated on, and letting them move drags the frozen galaxy render sub-pixel across the cusp, printing a core dipole.

knobs.code_doc: Per-component ellipticities in the refit (each Sersic + the MGE stack get their own e1/e2 -> isophote twist + radial flattening gradients; the shared-e model prints a quadrupolar residual). tonoise_v2 2026-07-19.
knobs.curated_html: Give each refit component (each Sersic and the MGE stack) its OWN ellipticity instead of one shared shape — allowing isophote twist and radial flattening gradients. A shared-ellipticity model of a real galaxy prints a characteristic quadrupolar residual; uncoupling removes it.

knobs.code_doc: Lensed point sources (quasar images). false = galaxy-galaxy mode.
knobs.curated_html: Whether the system contains multiply-imaged point sources (quasar images) to be modelled — the canonical time-delay-cosmography workflow. Set false for galaxy-galaxy strong lensing (extended source only). In that mode ALPACA skips point-source detection, the x_image/y_image/ps_amp latents, time-delay and ray-shooting likelihood factors, the entire PSF-reconstruction machinery (you must supply a fixed PSF), and point-source plot overlays.
warnings: With use_point_sources=false, config validation force-disables (with one grouped warning): psf.mode → "fixed", likelihood.use_time_delays, likelihood.use_rayshoot_consistency, likelihood.use_image_pos_offsets, likelihood.noise_model.noise_boost, and likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map — all of these need image positions or point-source flux to be meaningful.

knobs.code_doc: Render point sources by FFT convolution instead of direct PSF placement.
knobs.curated_html: Experimental (anomaly-005 fix): render point sources by exact Fourier-shift placement instead of the bilinear gather. The bilinear gather broadens every point-source core by a constant tent of ~1/3 native pixel; FFT placement removes that systematic at the cost of wrap-around edge behaviour.
warnings: Experimental — validate against a bilinear run before adopting for production H₀ inference.

knobs.code_doc: Fit a constant sky level.
knobs.curated_html: Add a uniform sky-background component to the lens light with a wide, data-driven prior on its amplitude (site sky_amp). Use when the cutout has an unsubtracted sky pedestal — otherwise that flux gets absorbed into profile wings and biases the lens-light (and thus source) decomposition.

knobs.code_doc: Fix the sky at this value (model units) instead of fitting it.

``"source_plane"`` (default, historical): the back-traced source positions of the images scatter around their mean with ``rayshoot_sigma`` (+ the optional free floor), and each delay uses its own back-traced position. ``"image_plane"``: one common source; the imaging centroids may differ from the lens-equation images by an image-plane Gaussian ``sigma_ast`` (mapped through each image's inverse-magnification matrix), the common source is the magnification-weighted mean, and all delays are evaluated for it (see :mod:`alpaca.models.astrometry`). Requires ``use_rayshoot_sys_error=False`` and ``use_image_pos_offsets=False``.

Prior sigma (arcsec) on per-image position offsets. ``None`` (default) resolves to 0.01 arcsec (10 mas), the astrometric precision of PSF-fitted quasar images in HST/JWST data. (It used to resolve to one native pixel, ~31 mas for NIRCam SW, which let the mass model largely ignore the quasar positions and biased D_dt.)
knobs.curated_html: Gaussian prior width on each per-image offset. About one native pixel is the sensible scale — much larger and the offsets can absorb genuine mass-model misfit instead of centroid noise.

knobs.code_doc: Boost the noise map around detected point sources so they don't dominate the extended-source fit.
knobs.curated_html: Multiplicatively boost the noise map in a circle around each detected point source, so PSF-core residuals at the bright quasar images don't dominate the extended-source and lens-light fit. The factor decays linearly from f_max at the PS centre to 1.0 at the boost radius.

knobs.code_doc: Keyword arguments forwarded to ``boost_noise_around_point_sources``.
knobs.curated_html:
Parameters forwarded to boost_noise_around_point_sources:

  • f_max — maximum multiplicative noise factor at the PS centre (1.0 = no boost).
  • radius — boost radius in arcsec; null = auto from PS separations.
  • frac_min_sep — auto radius = fraction × minimum PS separation.
  • min_npix / max_npix — clamps on the auto radius, in pixels.

knobs.code_doc: Factor the noise is multiplied by at the centre of each point-source image when `noise_boost` is on; it falls linearly to 1 at the boost radius (overlapping regions keep the maximum).
Fraction of the minimum separation between point-source images used as the automatic boost radius (when `radius` is null). Default 0.4.
Upper limit (pixels) of the automatic boost radius. Default 6.
Lower limit (pixels) of the automatic boost radius. Default 2.5.
Boost radius in arcsec. `null` (default) derives it from the image configuration: `frac_min_sep` × the smallest pairwise image separation, clipped to [`min_npix`, `max_npix`] pixels.

Upper bound of the Uniform(0, b_max) prior on the sampled ``b``. This is the anti-overfit cap: larger values let the likelihood down-weight the PS regions more aggressively (tonoise_v2 sweep, user 2026-07-19).
knobs.curated_html: Upper bound of the Uniform(0, b_max) prior on the sampled PSF-error amplitude b in σ²_eff = σ² + b²·ps_image². This is the anti-overfit cap: larger values let the likelihood down-weight the point-source regions more aggressively.
warnings: Check the FITTED b against this cap in the model summary — a b railing at b_max means the cap, not the data, is setting the point-source error budget, and the quoted fit quality inherits that choice.

knobs.code_doc: When/how the b term participates (validated in PipelineConfig): "joint"         - b free during GD and sampling (legacy). "post_gd_fixed" - b HELD AT 0 through GD stages 1-3; after stage 3 a 1-D exact fit of b at the frozen optimum (accounts for Poisson-noise underestimation at the PS cores); sampling runs with b FIXED at that value. "post_gd_free"  - same GD treatment; sampling has b FREE, warm-started at the post-GD fitted value (default: on HE0435 it reproduces the joint-b posterior with a better-converged, unboosted GD optimum).
Flux-scaling exponent p of the PSF-error term (1.0 = classic b^2 ps^2; p<1 re-weights the boost toward the PSF WINGS; tonoise_v2 2026-07-19).
Add a per-pixel variance term that scales with point-source flux: ``σ²_eff = σ² + b² · ps_image²`` where ``b`` is a sampled parameter.
knobs.curated_html: Add a per-pixel variance term scaling with point-source flux: σ²_eff = σ² + b² · ps_image², where b is a sampled Uniform(0, 0.1) parameter. A principled way to down-weight pixels where PSF-model errors dominate, letting the data infer how wrong the PSF is.

knobs.code_doc: If True, compare ray-traced positions to the sampled source position (``src_center_x/y``); if False, compare to the mean.
knobs.curated_html: If true, ray-traced image positions are compared against the sampled source-light centre (src_center_x/y) — coupling the point-source astrometry to the extended-source model. If false, they are compared against their own mean (pure internal consistency, decoupled from the light centroid).

knobs.code_doc: Astrometric uncertainty floor (arcsec) for the ray-shooting term.
knobs.curated_html: Astrometric uncertainty floor for the ray-shooting term — smaller values make the consistency constraint tighter. 0.001–0.002 is typical for HST/JWST astrometry. If set too small, the term dominates the imaging likelihood and GD can stall in astrometry-driven local minima; the free systematic-error parameter (use_rayshoot_sys_error) is the safer way to let the data pick the floor.

knobs.code_doc: (min, max) range (arcsec) for the systematic-error parameter.
knobs.curated_html: (min, max) of the log-uniform prior on the ray-shooting systematic error. 5×10⁻⁵ arcsec = 0.05 mas is at the floor of instrument astrometry; 5×10⁻³ arcsec = 5 mas is very loose. Widen the upper end for systems with visible astrometric anomalies.

knobs.code_doc: Image-plane astrometric perturbation (arcsec) for ``"image_plane"``.
Add per-image position offsets (TD + rayshoot terms only). Default False; when enabled, their prior width is ``image_pos_offset_sigma``.
knobs.curated_html: Sample per-image position offsets offset_{x,y}_image_{i} applied in the time-delay and ray-shooting terms — accounting for astrometric errors in the detected image centroids without moving the imaging-likelihood positions. One x/y pair per point-source image.
warnings: Force-disabled when light.point_sources.enabled=false.

knobs.code_doc: Add a penalty for scatter in ray-traced source positions.
knobs.curated_html: Add a penalty for scatter among the ray-traced source positions of the different point-source images — all images must trace back to the same source point. This is the imaging counterpart of the classical point-source astrometric likelihood and substantially tightens the mass model near the images.
warnings: Force-disabled when light.point_sources.enabled=false (no images to back-project).

knobs.code_doc: Sample a free systematic-error parameter for ray-shooting.
knobs.curated_html: Sample a free systematic-error parameter added to the ray-shooting uncertainty, with a log-uniform prior over rayshoot_sys_error_range. Lets the data decide the astrometric noise floor instead of trusting a fixed rayshoot_sigma — the robust choice when PSF residuals or microlensing may shift image centroids.

knobs.code_doc: Include the time-delay likelihood term.
knobs.curated_html:
Include the Gaussian time-delay likelihood term comparing predicted to measured delays between the point-source images. true is what makes the run an H₀ (D_dt) inference; false for imaging-only model comparison.

run_alpaca.py overrides this to false automatically when no TIME_DELAYS dict is provided, so the pipeline never demands missing data.

knobs.code_doc: How the deflection is evaluated.  ``"series"`` (default since 2026-09-26): closed-form homoeoid/Legendre series (:mod:`alpaca.models.bpl_series`) — same physics, more accurate than the quadrature at every axis ratio tested and ~3x cheaper per call. ``"quadrature"``: the original two-panel Gauss-Legendre evaluation.

``{"loc", "scale", "low", "high"}`` for a TruncatedNormal, the same shape as the EPL's ``gamma_prior``.  The default is deliberately WIDER than the EPL default (scale 0.3 vs 0.15): a broken profile splits the single well-constrained lensing slope between two parameters, so each is individually less constrained and a tight prior would just re-impose the EPL answer.
knobs.curated_html: TruncatedNormal prior on the INNER slope (same shape as the EPL's gamma_prior; bpl.gamma_out is the outer twin). Deliberately WIDER than the EPL default (scale 0.3 vs 0.15): a broken profile splits the single well-constrained lensing slope between two parameters, and a tight prior would just re-impose the EPL answer.

knobs.code_doc: Upper truncation of the γ_in prior (default 2.7).

Centre of the TruncatedNormal prior on the INNER slope γ_in of the broken power law (default 2.0). The BPL priors are deliberately wider than the EPL's: the single, well-constrained lensing slope is split between two parameters.
Lower truncation of the γ_in prior (default 1.3).
Width of the TruncatedNormal prior on γ_in (default 0.3; the EPL uses 0.15).

``{"loc", "scale", "low", "high"}`` for a TruncatedNormal, the same shape as the EPL's ``gamma_prior``.  The default is deliberately WIDER than the EPL default (scale 0.3 vs 0.15): a broken profile splits the single well-constrained lensing slope between two parameters, so each is individually less constrained and a tight prior would just re-impose the EPL answer.
knobs.curated_html: TruncatedNormal prior on the OUTER slope — the twin of mass.main.bpl.gamma_in (see that entry for why the priors are deliberately wide). Sub-keys: loc/scale are the Normal centre and width, low/high the truncation bounds.

knobs.code_doc: Upper truncation of the γ_out prior (default 2.7).
Centre of the TruncatedNormal prior on the OUTER slope γ_out (default 2.0). γ_in = γ_out reproduces the EPL exactly.
Lower truncation of the γ_out prior (default 1.3).
Width of the γ_out prior (default 0.3).

Gauss-Legendre nodes PER PANEL (two panels, split at the break) for the deflection and the potential.  See :mod:`alpaca.models.mass_profiles` — 24/28 gives ~1e-13 relative accuracy for a round-to-mildly-flattened deflector and stays below 1e-6 down to q ~ 0.5.  Lower only if profiling says so.  Used for the potential always, and for the deflection only when ``deflection == "quadrature"``.
knobs.curated_html: Gauss-Legendre nodes PER PANEL (two panels, split analytically at the break) for the BPL deflection; n_quad_potential (default 28) is the potential's counterpart. 24 reproduces the analytic EPL to ~1e-13 at γ=2 (where the endpoint substitution makes the quadrature exact) and stays below 1e-6 relative down to q~0.55. Lower only if profiling says so.

knobs.code_doc: Gauss-Legendre nodes PER PANEL (two panels, split at the break) for the deflection and the potential.  See :mod:`alpaca.models.mass_profiles` — 24/28 gives ~1e-13 relative accuracy for a round-to-mildly-flattened deflector and stays below 1e-6 down to q ~ 0.5.  Lower only if profiling says so.  Used for the potential always, and for the deflection only when ``deflection == "quadrature"``.
Terms of each series (the two EPL pieces and the core term).  They converge like ((1-q)/(1+q))^n; 40 keeps the error below 1e-13" for q >= 0.3 and below the quadrature's everywhere down to q = 0.2.
``[low, high]`` bounds of the Uniform prior on ``r_break/theta_E``.
knobs.curated_html: Uniform prior bounds on the break radius in units of θE (site lens_r_break_frac). Tying the break to θ_E keeps it inside the annulus the arcs actually constrain for every sample, instead of letting the chain wander into a regime where the second slope is unconstrained.

knobs.code_doc: Width [arcsec] of the Normal prior of the mass centre around the (detected / given) lens-light centre. None = mode default: 0.3" when point sources anchor the mass (quasar mode), 0.05" without them (galaxy-galaxy mode), where nothing else ties the mass to the lens and multistarts otherwise settle on a small-theta_E "lens" on an arc image.

If True use the ELLIPTICAL multipoles of Paugnat & Gilman (2025) (lenstronomy's ``MULTIPOLE_ELL``, :class:`alpaca.models.multipole_ell.MultipoleEllCS`) instead of the default circular ones: the perturbation then deforms the main deflector's own elliptical isodensity contours, sharing its axis ratio and position angle, and the phase is measured from its major axis.  Only ``m = 1, 3, 4`` are implemented.  Default False (the circular :class:`MultipoleCS`, unchanged behaviour).
Multipole orders to include, e.g. ``[1, 3, 4]``.  Empty (default) = no multipoles, i.e. the historical EPL+SHEAR model.  ``m = 2`` is NOT recommended: it is degenerate with the EPL ellipticity.
knobs.curated_html:
Angular multipole orders added to the main deflector, e.g. [3, 4]. Each order m adds the convergence κ_m = a_m·cos[m(φ−φ_m)]/(2r) and TWO sampled sites, the Cartesian pair lens_a{m}_cos/lens_a{m}_sin (single-valued and smooth through zero — the polar (a_m, φ_m) pair is 2m-fold multimodal and singular exactly at the a_m=0 null-test point). All amplitudes zero = the EPL, bit-for-bit.

m=4 is boxy/discy — the mode with real photometric backing (a₄/a ~ 1–2% in ellipticals). m=3 is the triangular mode. m=1 is supported (it needs a special r·ln r potential — the scale-free form divides by zero) but see the warning.

knobs.code_doc: Reference radius (arcsec) in the ``m = 1`` potential ``psi = (1/2) r ln(r/r_ref) C(phi)``.  Changing it only adds a CONSTANT deflection (degenerate with the source position) and does not touch the convergence; it is fixed rather than sampled so the ``m = 1`` amplitudes stay well conditioned.  Default 1.0" ~ theta_E.
knobs.curated_html: Reference radius (arcsec) in the m=1 potential ψ₁ = ½·r·ln(r/r_ref)·C(φ). Changing it only adds a CONSTANT deflection — exactly degenerate with a source-plane shift, leaving the convergence untouched — so it is held fixed (~θ_E) rather than sampled. Ignored without m=1.

knobs.code_doc: Width of the zero-mean Normal prior on each Cartesian amplitude, in arcsec.  A dict maps order -> sigma (keys may be ints or strings), any missing order falling back to ``sigma_default``. Scale intuition: the convergence perturbation is ``kappa_m = a_m cos(m(phi-phi_m)) / (2 r)``, so ``a_m / theta_E`` is the usual dimensionless multipole strength.  Real ellipticals have ``a_4/a ~ 0.01-0.02``; for a ``theta_E ~ 1"`` lens the default ``sigma = 0.02"`` is a weakly informative ~1.7% prior that still lets the data push to ~5% amplitudes.
knobs.curated_html: Width (arcsec) of the zero-mean Normal prior on each Cartesian amplitude; a dict maps order → σ with sigma_default as fallback. The example uses null, so every configured order delegates to sigma_default = 0.02. Scale intuition: a_m/θ_E is the usual dimensionless strength; real ellipticals sit at 0.01–0.02, so σ=0.02" (~2% of a typical θ_E) is weakly informative and lets the data push to ~5%.

knobs.code_doc: Fallback width when ``sigma`` is a dict without that order.
knobs.curated_html: Fallback prior width used for any multipole order not listed when multipoles.sigma is a per-order dict (or when it is null).

knobs.code_doc: Radial profile of the main deflector.  ``"epl"`` (default) is the historical elliptical power law with a single ``lens_gamma``; ``"bpl"`` is the elliptical broken power law (see :class:`BrokenPowerLawConfig`).
knobs.curated_html:
Radial mass profile of the main deflector.

  • "EPL+Shear" — elliptical power law + external shear, one slope lens_gamma. The historical model (legacy alias "epl").
  • "BPL+Shear" — elliptical broken power law + external shear (legacy alias "bpl"): slope gamma_in inside a break radius, gamma_out outside. Samples lens_gamma_in, lens_gamma_out, lens_r_break_frac and removes lens_gamma. Reduces to the EPL exactly at gamma_in = gamma_out (verified to ~1e-13), and θE keeps its EPL meaning (mean convergence 1 inside θE) so the two models are directly comparable.

The BPL has no closed-form deflection — it is evaluated by desingularised Gauss-Legendre quadrature (Keeton 2001), costing ~×1.8 per gradient.

The profile string selects the RADIAL model only — angular structure is added independently via mass.main.multipoles.orders (combinable with either profile), and the external shear is always part of the model.

knobs.code_doc: {center, sigma} in arcsec: TruncatedNormal prior on the Einstein radius. Required for galaxy-galaxy lenses.
knobs.curated_html: Optional informative prior on the main-lens Einstein radius. null keeps the wide Uniform(0.5 r_min, 1.5 r_max) driven by the detected image positions. {"center": <arcsec>, "sigma": <arcsec>} samples theta_E from a TruncatedNormal clipped to the same physical bounds — useful to test whether pinning theta_E to an external measurement changes the fit or the outer-arc residual.

Fiducial H₀ for the multi-plane distance-ratio (η) matrix and the fiducial time-delay distance used to rescale multi-plane arrival times onto the sampled D_dt. Distance ratios are exactly H₀-independent, so this choice does not bias the H₀ inference — it is the standard treatment.
Fiducial matter density for the multi-plane distance ratios. The dependence of the ratios on Ω_m is weak; 0.3 is the conventional choice.

knobs.curated_html: "auto" gives honest plane assignment: perturbers within z_tolerance of the lens redshift join the main plane as ordinary profiles; the rest get their own fore-/background planes, switching to multi-plane ray tracing with distance ratios fixed at the fiducial cosmology and arrival times rescaled by the sampled D_dt. When set, each selected perturber contributes its catalog-declared mass profile; perturbers outside the main-plane redshift window get their own planes and switch the forward model to multi-plane lensing (Herculens MPLensImage).

Per-dataset path — prefer setting it via PERTURBERS_PATH in run_alpaca.py.

Shrinking to 61–81 restricts the fit to the signal-carrying PSF core and stops the background grid from absorbing wing noise.

knobs.curated_html: Upper bound of the Uniform(0, b_max) prior on psf_error_b during the reconstruction stage only. Raising it to 0.3–0.5 gives the likelihood more room to absorb PSF mis-modelling in early iterations when the initial PSF is crude. Restored before multistart + sampling.

Automatically reverts before multistart MAP and posterior sampling, which then see the user's global ``likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map`` setting unchanged. Independent of that global flag: if both are True, this one is a no-op (PSF stage already has the error map).

Down-weights point-source cores in the internal GD so the lens/source/lens-light fit isn't starved by PSF-mismodelling leverage, giving STARRED cleaner model-subtracted stamps. Automatically reverted before multistart MAP and sampling, which see the global likelihood.noise_model.use_psf_error_map unchanged.

knobs.curated_html: When fitting each point source in STARRED, mask the other detected peaks so a neighbouring image's flux doesn't contaminate the stamp. Essential for small-separation quads.

knobs.code_doc: Radius (pixels) of the mask around other peaks.
knobs.curated_html: Radius of the mask placed over each contaminant peak. Should comfortably cover the neighbour's PSF core without eating the stamp being fitted.

knobs.code_doc: Window-function shape for the contaminant-PS masks fed to STARRED. ``"cosine"`` (default) applies a raised-cosine taper outside ``radius_pix`` over a width ``smoothing_width_pix``, suppressing the Fourier-domain ringing that a hard 0/1 cut would inject into the PSF reconstruction. ``"hard"`` reproduces the legacy 0/1 binary mask. ``"gaussian"`` uses ``1 - exp(-r^2 / (2 * R^2))`` with ``R = radius_pix``.
knobs.curated_html: Window shape of the contaminant masks fed to STARRED. "cosine" applies a raised-cosine taper outside radius_pix over smoothing_width_pix, suppressing the Fourier-domain ringing a hard 0/1 edge injects into the reconstruction. "hard" reproduces the legacy binary mask; "gaussian" uses 1 − exp(−r²/2R²) with R = radius_pix.

knobs.code_doc: Width (pixels) of the cosine taper. Ignored when ``smoothing != "cosine"``.
knobs.curated_html: Width of the raised-cosine taper. Ignored unless smoothing="cosine". Must be non-negative (validated).

knobs.code_doc: Number of iterative PSF refinement passes.
knobs.curated_html: Number of outer refinement passes: fit lens model → subtract extended light → re-fit PSF on the cleaned point sources → repeat. Two passes usually converge; more help when the initial PSF is very approximate.

knobs.code_doc: Random starts for multi-start optimization per iteration.
knobs.curated_html: Random starts for the internal lens-modelling multi-start inside each PSF iteration. Higher = more robust extended-light subtraction (and thus cleaner PSF stamps), slower.

knobs.code_doc: Clip pixels below ``-negative_sigma_clip * σ`` in the reconstructed PSF. ``None`` disables clipping.
knobs.curated_html: Clip reconstructed PSF pixels below −N × σ — masking negative reconstruction artefacts that would imprint dark rings around every point source. null disables clipping.

knobs.code_doc: Parallelize multi-start evaluations across devices.
knobs.curated_html: Parallelize the multi-start evaluations across available devices (GPUs). Disable only for debugging or on memory-starved single-GPU nodes.

knobs.code_doc: Rotation augmentation mode for STARRED.
knobs.curated_html: Rotation augmentation inside STARRED: "90" adds a 90°-rotated copy of each stamp, "all" every 90° rotation. Augmentation suppresses detector-frame systematics at the cost of imprinting rotational symmetry on the kernel — leave "none" for PSFs with strong diffraction spikes.

knobs.code_doc: Supersampling factor inside STARRED. ``None`` (default) inherits ``psf.input.oversample`` so the reconstruction works on the same grid as the input PSF.
knobs.curated_html: Internal supersampling factor of the STARRED reconstruction grid. The reconstructed kernel is returned at this resolution relative to native pixels.

knobs.code_doc: Convolution backend for the live kernel ("fft").
knobs.curated_html: Convolution backend for the live kernel. "fft" is the supported production choice; direct convolution is orders of magnitude slower for typical kernel sizes.

knobs.code_doc: Which PSF blocks are free GD latents.
knobs.curated_html: Which PSF blocks become free GD latents. "moffat" frees the analytic core (FWHM, β, ellipticity C, angle φ); "background" frees the STARRED pixel grid that carries diffraction structure and wings. Freeing both gives the most faithful kernel but adds the full grid as latents — the background prior configuration below then matters a lot.

knobs.code_doc: Supersampling factor of the live joint kernel (STARRED grid). Fallback when the seed does not record its own ``upsampling_factor``. ``None`` (default) inherits ``psf.input.oversample`` — the joint kernel lives on the same grid as the input PSF.
knobs.curated_html: Supersampling factor of the live joint kernel (the STARRED grid). Used as a fallback when the seed file does not record its own upsampling_factor — a seed that records it wins.

knobs.code_doc: Global scale on the measured error map (``type == "error_map"``).
knobs.curated_html: Global scale on the measured error map in the "error_map" recipe. 1.0 trusts the map as-is; > 1 inflates the prior widths if the map is known to be optimistic (e.g. it omits systematic terms).

knobs.code_doc: Numerical floor added to the per-pixel width (heuristic and error_map recipes). ``None`` -> 5% of the seed background std.
knobs.curated_html: Numerical floor added to the per-pixel width (heuristic and error_map recipes). Guards against σᵢ → 0 in the zero-error wings, which would freeze those pixels and can condition the optimisation badly. null uses 5% of the seed background's standard deviation.

knobs.code_doc: Non-centered reparametrization of the free background grid (b = seed + sigma*z, z~N(0,1)). Identical prior, well-conditioned geometry for tiny sigma. Set False for the original centered behaviour.
knobs.curated_html: Non-centered reparametrization of the free background grid: b = seed + σ·z with z ~ N(0,1) as the latent. The prior is identical, but the geometry is far better conditioned when σ is tiny (as it is with a measured error map) — recommended whenever the background is free.

knobs.code_doc: Relative width for the heuristic recipe.
knobs.curated_html: Relative width for the "heuristic" recipe: σᵢ = rel × |seedᵢ| + floor. Larger values let bright background pixels move more.

knobs.code_doc: Global scalar width; required when ``type == "scalar"``.
knobs.curated_html: Global scalar width for the "scalar" recipe — one σ for every background pixel.

knobs.code_doc: Space the error-map prior acts in: ``"background"`` (legacy: width on the bg latent) or ``"kernel"`` (Gaussian prior on the full PSF kernel via a factor — the physically correct space; no deconvolution of the narrow->full convolution needed).
knobs.curated_html: Space the error-map prior acts in. "kernel" places a Gaussian prior on the full PSF kernel via a likelihood factor — the physically correct space, since the error map measures kernel uncertainty (and no deconvolution of the narrow→full convolution is needed). "background" is the legacy behaviour: the width is applied directly to the background latent.

knobs.code_doc: Which prior-width recipe to use (see above).
knobs.curated_html:
Recipe for the per-pixel prior width on the free STARRED background grid (only consulted when "background" is in psf.joint.free):

  • "heuristic" — σᵢ = rel × |seedᵢ| + floor: freedom proportional to the seed's own structure.
  • "error_map" — σᵢ = sqrt((α × errmapᵢ)² + floor²): the measured uncertainty of the seed PSF, read from psf.input.error_map_path. The physically motivated choice when you have an empirical error map.
  • "scalar" — one global σ for every pixel.

knobs.code_doc: Absolute Normal(0, sigma) prior for the Moffat angle phi (whose seed is ~0).
knobs.curated_html: Absolute Normal(0, σ) prior on the Moffat position angle φ, whose seed value is ~0 (a relative width would collapse to zero there).

knobs.code_doc: Moffat priors: Normal(seed, rel*|seed|) for fwhm/beta/C.
knobs.curated_html: Relative prior width on the Moffat core parameters: Normal(seed, rel × |seed|) for FWHM, β and the ellipticity parameter C. 0.1 = 10% freedom around the seed — enough to correct a slightly wrong STARRED fit while anchoring the core against source–PSF degeneracy.
Starlet regularization strength on the highest-frequency scale — the main defence against the background grid absorbing pixel noise.

Penalty on negative kernel pixels. The shipped value (10⁶) makes positivity effectively a hard constraint; the small dataclass default only nudges. Negative PSF pixels imprint dark rings around every point source, so a strong positivity term is usually right.
STARRED-style starlet regularization strength on the coarse wavelet scales of the live kernel — suppresses smooth spurious structure the imaging likelihood can't constrain.
warnings: The lambdas here are unnormalised (no star noise-map W), so values tuned inside STARRED/JWSTPSF do not transfer 1:1 — calibrate empirically on your data.

knobs.code_doc: Path to the JWSTPSF/STARRED seed (kwargs_moffat + kwargs_background). Required in joint mode.
knobs.curated_html: Path to the STARRED/JWSTPSF seed containing kwargs_moffat (analytic core) and kwargs_background (pixel grid), produced by a PSF fit you ran ahead of time. The seed centres the priors of the free PSF blocks and provides the frozen parts. Per-dataset path — prefer setting it via PSF_STARRED_KWARGS_PATH in run_alpaca.py.

knobs.code_doc: When True, allow ``psf.input.oversample > 1`` in joint mode so the bright point-source cores are rendered with a LIVE supersampled (high-res) joint PSF kernel (Moffat fit at os-resolution; STARRED background built on the os grid). Extended light stays on the static supersampled SubgridKernelConvolution path (seed HR kernel). Requires ``data.source_oversample == psf.input.oversample``. Set False for the native-only joint behaviour.
knobs.curated_html: Allow psf.input.oversample > 1 in joint mode: bright point-source cores are rendered with a live supersampled joint kernel (Moffat evaluated at the oversampled resolution; STARRED background built on the oversampled grid), while extended light stays on the static supersampled convolution path using the seed high-res kernel. Set this to false for native-resolution-only joint behaviour.

The single source of truth for how the PSF is treated:

  • "fixed" — trust the PSF you provide; no reconstruction at all. Only the psf.input section matters.
  • "iterative" — iteratively reconstruct the PSF with STARRED before the main gradient descent (settings under psf.iterative).
  • "joint" — fit the PSF (Moffat core + optional background grid) jointly with the lens model during gradient descent, seeded from a STARRED/JWSTPSF fit (settings under psf.joint).

The subsection not matching the mode is ignored; if an ignored section differs from its defaults, a notice is printed so a stale section can't silently mislead. The legacy layout (run_psf, mode="joint_gd", flat psf.joint_* keys) is auto-upgraded with a deprecation notice.

knobs.code_doc: Run the gradient-descent stages (MAP).
knobs.curated_html: Run the multi-start gradient-descent MAP stage (03_multistart/). Nearly always true — the MAP point seeds the sampler, defines the signal-derived arc mask, and (in joint PSF mode) carries the PSF fit. Set false only to start sampling directly from prior means or from a previous run's best fit.

knobs.code_doc: Directory for all outputs of this run. A new directory per model variant: re-running into an existing directory resumes it.
knobs.curated_html: Root directory for all pipeline outputs (input snapshots, PSF stage, multistart, sampling, plots, timing). The literal token {date} is replaced with a YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM timestamp when the config is built, so every run lands in its own sub-folder. A trailing slash is added if missing; an empty string, null, or an omitted key falls back to pipeline_output (the {date} expansion only happens in the run scripts, so the dataclass deliberately does not default to the {date} path).
warnings: Resume logic (staged joint-PSF stages, resume_from_previous) keys off directories inside output_dir — reuse the same directory (no {date} token) if you want reruns to skip completed stages.

knobs.code_doc: Seed for every random choice (multistart draws, perturbations, sampler).
knobs.curated_html: Master PRNG seed, propagated to every stochastic component: multi-start initial positions, Adam/L-BFGS randomness, sampler chains, posterior subsampling. Fixing it makes runs bit-reproducible on the same hardware/software stack; change it to probe run-to-run scatter of the multistart.

knobs.code_doc: Skip GD and load a previous MAP (for sampling only).
knobs.curated_html: Only consulted when run.multistart=false: if true, load the best-fit parameters from a previous run's 03_multistart/ directory and use them as the sampling start point; if false, start from prior means.
warnings: The loaded best fit must come from a compatible model — the staged flow fingerprints the likelihood config and warns (and invalidates later stages) when the objective changed, e.g. a time-delay flip.

knobs.code_doc: Folder of the previous 03_multistart to load when resuming.
knobs.curated_html: Explicit path to a previous run's 03_multistart/ directory. When null, the path is derived from output_dir. Only used when resume_from_previous=true.

knobs.code_doc: Run posterior sampling after the GD stages.
knobs.curated_html: Run posterior sampling (NUTS / Nautilus / NIFTy) after gradient descent. Disable to stop after the MAP stage — useful for quick model checks, arc-mask tuning, or PSF-stage debugging where the posterior is not needed yet.

knobs.code_doc: Print progress to stdout.
knobs.curated_html: Master verbosity toggle applied to every pipeline stage — progress prints, per-start GD summaries, sampler diagnostics. Does not affect what is written to disk, only console output.

knobs.code_doc: When True (NIFTy + staged joint-PSF only), the PSF Moffat-core parameters remain FREE latents during posterior sampling, so the posterior marginalises over PSF uncertainty instead of freezing the kernel at the final GD value. The background grid stays frozen at its GD value (the 447^2 grid is intractable as VI latents and is pinned by the error-map floor). Requires the staged joint-PSF model (joint_stages set). Set False to reproduce the legacy frozen-kernel sampling exactly.
knobs.curated_html: Keep the PSF Moffat-core parameters as free latents during posterior sampling, so the posterior marginalises over PSF uncertainty instead of freezing the kernel at the final GD value. The background grid stays frozen at its GD value (a ~450² grid is intractable as VI latents and is pinned by the error-map floor). Default false reproduces legacy frozen-kernel sampling exactly.

knobs.code_doc: When marginalize_psf is on, ALSO marginalise the PSF background — but only the high-res pixels inside a central box of side ~ marginalize_psf_background_fwhm_box * fwhm * upsampling (where the PSF carries signal), as a perturbation around the GD-recovered grid. Keeps the sampled-background latent count tiny (= side**2) so geoVI/NUTS stays tractable; the kernel-space prior anchors it to the measured error map. Set False to freeze the whole background (legacy marginalize_psf).
knobs.curated_html: When marginalize_psf is on, also marginalise the PSF background — but only the high-res pixels inside a central box of side ≈ fwhm_box × fwhm × upsampling, where the PSF actually carries signal, sampled as a perturbation around the GD-recovered grid. Keeps the sampled-background latent count tiny (= side²) so geoVI/NUTS stays tractable; the kernel-space prior anchors it to the measured error map.
warnings: Meaningless without sampling.marginalize_psf=true.

knobs.code_doc: Must stay small enough that side = fwhm_box * fwhm * upsampling is below image_size_up; otherwise the box clips to the full grid and the latent count is image_size_up**2 rather than tiny.
knobs.curated_html: Size of the marginalised background box, in units of the PSF FWHM (times the upsampling factor), giving a box of side fwhm_box × fwhm × upsampling centred on the kernel. Only pixels inside the box become free latents. The side is clipped to the full high-res grid, so once fwhm_box × fwhm × upsampling reaches image_size_up, the box covers every background pixel. The example value of 80.0 therefore resolves to the full high-resolution grid if background marginalisation is enabled; in the worked run it is dormant because marginalize_psf is false.

knobs.code_doc: Target posterior sample count after final subsampling. ``None`` keeps whatever the backend produced (no resampling) — with a finite target, backends that produced fewer raw draws than the target are resampled WITH replacement up to it.
knobs.curated_html: Target posterior sample count after final subsampling — the size of the chains written to posterior_samples.npz and used by corner plots and downstream cosmography.
Likelihood-evaluation batch size per device. Larger batches amortise dispatch overhead until memory limits bite.
Number of live points. More live points improve evidence accuracy and multimodal coverage at proportional cost.
Map the unit cube through uniform priors (Nautilus' native parametrisation) rather than the model's transformed priors.
Evaluate the likelihood through the JAX-compiled path (batched, GPU-accelerated) instead of plain NumPy calls.
Distribute batched likelihood evaluations across all available devices.

knobs.code_doc: NIFTy sub-mode, consulted only when the effective sampler is ``"nifty"``.
knobs.curated_html:
NIFTy sub-mode, consulted only when the effective sampler is "nifty":

  • "vi+nuts" — geoVI first, then NUTS-in-ξ refinement warm-started from it. Asymptotically exact, and enables the VI-derived mass matrices.
  • "vi_only" — geoVI only. Fast, but a Gaussian (in ξ) approximation.
  • "nuts_only" — NUTS-in-ξ warm-started from the gradient-descent MAP, skipping VI entirely.

Chain execution strategy. "auto" (the default) picks "parallel" when num_chains ≥ device_count > 1, otherwise "vectorized" — batching all chains into one XLA program, which is roughly a wall-clock factor of num_chains faster than running them one at a time. There is an automatic OOM fallback to "sequential", so "auto" is safe to leave on; set "sequential" explicitly only to force the memory-safe path up front. Note that models above 50000 latent dimensions are routed to a per-chain collector regardless of this setting.

knobs.code_doc: For mass_matrix="block_from_vi": the ξ-leaf names that form the single DENSE block of the mass matrix (everything else stays diagonal). The block is seeded with the geoVI sample COVARIANCE of these leaves, capturing the macro-lens correlations (slope / θ_E / shear / D_dt) that a diagonal mass matrix throws away. None -> the built-in macro-lens default set. Names not present among the live latents are silently skipped.
knobs.curated_html: For mass_matrix="block_from_vi": the ξ-leaf names forming the single dense block (everything else stays diagonal). null uses the built-in macro-lens default set; names not present among the live latents are silently skipped.
Gaussian jitter applied to each chain's initial position — keeps all chains on the typical set (near the warm start) while making them distinguishable, so R-hat is meaningful.

Mass matrix for ξ-space NUTS:

  • "identity" — no adaptation; canonical for standardised ξ-space, but ignores likelihood-induced scale differences.
  • "adaptive_diag" — NumPyro's Welford diagonal estimator during warmup. Robust general default.
  • "diag_from_vi" — per-coordinate variances from the geoVI residual samples.
  • "block_from_vi" — dense macro-lens block seeded from the geoVI sample covariance (slope / θ_E / shear / D_dt correlations that a diagonal matrix throws away), diagonal elsewhere.
Maximum NUTS trajectory tree depth (2^depth leapfrog steps). Chains persistently hitting the cap signal a bad mass matrix — fix that before raising the cap (each +1 doubles the worst-case cost).
Number of chains; null = one per GPU with a minimum of 2, so R-hat is always defined.
Post-warmup samples per chain.
Warmup iterations per chain for NUTS in ξ-space. ξ-space is prior-standardised, but the likelihood still bends it — generous warmup pays off for CF+PSF models.
Target acceptance for step-size adaptation. Raise if divergences appear.
Variational algorithm: "MGVI" (metric Gaussian VI — faster, Gaussian approximation in ξ) or "geoVI" (geometric VI — adapts to posterior curvature, more accurate for non-Gaussian posteriors).
Conjugate-gradient iterations for linear sample draws and KL minimisation. Higher values give more accurate VI samples per iteration at linear cost — the shipped 100 prioritises accuracy.
Scale factor of the random initial position in latent (ξ) space around the warm start.
Total VI outer iterations (KL-minimisation rounds). Watch the reported KL/energy: if it is still falling at the end, add iterations.

knobs.code_doc: batch-resample from converged geoVI; 0 = skip
knobs.curated_html: Batch-resample count from the converged geoVI approximation (posterior samples beyond the few used during convergence). 0 disables and keeps only the convergence samples.
warnings: Ignored when NUTS refinement follows (nifty.mode="vi+nuts") — the NUTS samples overwrite these anyway.

knobs.curated_html: Antithetic sample pairs drawn per VI iteration for the KL estimate. A fixed value is safest; null switches to an adaptive schedule (4→8→16→64).
warnings: The adaptive schedule (null) can OOM on large correlated fields — the late-stage 64-sample rounds are memory-hungry. Prefer a fixed value on big grids.

knobs.curated_html: Fast settings for testing/debugging — reduces conjugate-gradient iteration counts. Not for production posteriors.
PRNG keys per resampling batch; mirror (antithetic) sampling doubles each batch.
Shard the geoVI computation across all GPUs to reduce per-GPU memory — often the difference between fitting and OOM for 128²+ correlated fields.

knobs.code_doc: Stop when the gradient norm of U falls below this.
L-BFGS iteration cap.

``"lbfgs"`` (default): optax L-BFGS with zoom line search on U until ``|grad U| < gtol`` or ``maxiter`` iterations; kept only if U decreased and stayed finite. ``"off"``: the bare exact transfer (0.4.1 behaviour).

knobs.curated_html: Number of chains. null runs one chain per available device. At least 2 chains are needed for meaningful R-hat diagnostics.
Post-warmup samples per chain.
Warmup (adaptation) iterations per chain — step size and mass-matrix tuning. Lens posteriors with strong D_dt–slope correlations benefit from generous warmup.
Target acceptance probability for the dual-averaging step-size adaptation. Raise towards 0.9–0.95 if divergences appear (smaller steps, slower sampling).

knobs.code_doc: Backend. ``"default"`` auto-selects: NIFTy for correlated-field models, Nautilus for ≤50 parameters, NUTS otherwise.
knobs.curated_html:
Posterior sampling backend:

  • "nuts" — classical NumPyro NUTS on the physical parameters. Right for Shapelets/Sersic models with moderate dimensionality.
  • "nautilus" — nested sampling. Practical up to ~50 parameters and the only backend that returns a log-evidence (model comparison).
  • "nifty" — NIFTy-based inference (geoVI and/or NUTS in ξ-space). Required for correlated-field sources; also the backend that supports PSF marginalisation.
  • "default" — auto-select: NIFTy for correlated fields, Nautilus for ≤ 50 parameters, NUTS otherwise.
warnings: Nautilus does not scale past ~50 parameters — with image-position offsets, perturbers and a large Shapelet basis you can exceed that quickly; check the printed parameter count.

knobs.code_doc: Learning rate of the joint stage.
knobs.curated_html: Adam learning rate for stage 3.

knobs.code_doc: Adam steps of the joint CorrField stage.
knobs.curated_html: Adam steps in stage 3 (cf_joint): a single-start joint optimisation with all latents free (CF source, lens, point sources, PSF), started from the stage-2 state.

knobs.code_doc: Run the CorrField joint stage (stage 3): source, lens, lens light and PSF fitted together.
knobs.curated_html: Run the joint CF stage: source + mass (+ PSF in joint-PSF mode, + lens light per stages.cf_joint.lens_light) optimised together, warm-started from the previous stages. This is the stage that produces the MAP model the sampler is centred on. With both CF stages disabled the pipeline is shapelets-only: sampling runs on the stage-1 model.

knobs.code_doc: Optional L-BFGS polish after the joint Adam (0 = off).
knobs.curated_html: Optional L-BFGS polish after the stage-3 Adam run; 0 disables. A few hundred iterations can sharpen the MAP before sampling, at the risk of L-BFGS instabilities on the high-dimensional CF+PSF objective.

knobs.code_doc: 'free' or 'fixed': whether the lens light from the refit stays free in stage 3.
knobs.curated_html: NEW (2026-08-18): whether the cf_joint stage optimises against the refit's FROZEN lens light (historical behaviour — all ~27 refit sites substituted) or leaves the lens light FREE as sampled latents. runtime knob: light.lens.refit.freeze_in_cf_joint.
warnings: With "free" the lens light initialises from STAGE 1, not from the refit values — the refit still runs and saves its outputs, but enters cf_joint's start only via the warm-start flow.

knobs.code_doc: Prior centre of the live PSF in stage 3: 'seed' (STARRED seed) or 'stage1'.
knobs.curated_html: PSF prior centering in stage 3. "seed" keeps the identical prior used in stage 1 (centred on the STARRED seed). "stage1" re-centres the Moffat/background/kernel prior means on the stage-1 recovered PSF (sigmas unchanged) — a trust region around the stage-1 kernel that limits CF↔PSF degeneracy excursions when the flexible source could otherwise trade flux with the PSF wings.

knobs.code_doc: Whether to adapt the source grid extent to the arc mask.
knobs.curated_html: Adapt the source-plane grid extent to the ray-shot arc mask, so field pixels cover the region the arcs actually map to instead of a fixed window. Disable only for controlled comparisons with fixed-grid runs.

knobs.code_doc: Path to a custom mask (FITS or ``.npy``) when mode == "custom".
knobs.curated_html: Path to a custom boolean arc mask (FITS or .npy, matching the image shape). Only read when mode="custom".

knobs.code_doc: Inner radius (arcsec) to mask the lens centre. ``"auto"`` computes from PS positions.
knobs.curated_html: Inner radius masking out the lens centre (lens-light-dominated region). "auto" computes 0.6 × r_min_ps from the innermost point-source radius. 0 disables the central hole — appropriate when the lens light is well modelled and the arcs pass close to the centre.

knobs.code_doc: "auto" = circular annulus from PS positions; "signal" = derived from GD residuals; "custom" = load from ``custom_path``.
knobs.curated_html:
How the arc mask (the image-plane region where the source model is evaluated / the CF grid is anchored) is built:

  • "auto" — circular annulus derived from the point-source positions. Safe default; needs no prior fit.
  • "signal" — derived from gradient-descent residuals: pixels above an SNR threshold, dilated and cleaned. Tightest mask, best CF resolution.
  • "custom" — load a user-provided mask from custom_path.

knobs.code_doc: Outer radius (arcsec) for the source region. ``"auto"`` computes from PS positions.
knobs.curated_html: Outer radius of the source region. "auto" computes 2.0 × r_max_ps from the outermost point-source radius — generous enough for typical quads while excluding field contaminants.

knobs.code_doc: Morphological dilation radius in pixels.
knobs.curated_html: Morphological dilation radius applied to the thresholded signal mask, padding it to include low-SNR arc outskirts adjacent to detected pixels.

knobs.code_doc: Inner radius = ``factor * r_min_ps`` (smaller = let signal decide).
knobs.curated_html: Inner-radius factor for signal mode: a geometric hole of factor × r_min_ps is intersected with the signal mask. The default 0 lets the signal mask alone define the arc, with no central exclusion.

knobs.code_doc: Minimum connected-component area (pixels).
knobs.curated_html: Minimum connected-component area in the signal mask; smaller blobs (noise islands, hot pixels) are removed. Lower it if a genuinely small counter-image is being erased.

knobs.code_doc: SNR threshold for arc detection (mode == "signal" only).
knobs.curated_html: SNR threshold for a residual pixel to enter the signal-derived mask (mode "signal" only). Lower it to catch faint outer arc segments at the cost of noise blobs — which the dilation and minimum-area cleanup then have to remove.

knobs.code_doc: Optional spectral priors. ``None`` disables.
knobs.curated_html: Optional NIFTy spectral prior on the roughness of the power spectrum itself (wiggliness on top of flexibility). null disables; only meaningful together with flexibility.

knobs.code_doc: Legacy source-image truncation is separate from adaptive-grid selection. False keeps PSF-spread source light outside the footprint in the model.
Border pixels cropped to mitigate FFT edge effects.
knobs.curated_html: Border pixels cropped from the field to mitigate FFT periodic-boundary artefacts (the GP is defined on a torus). The field is evaluated on num_pixels + 2·border per side and then cropped back to num_pixels, so the effective source grid stays num_pixels while the sampled latent block is (num_pixels + 2·border)². Increase if bright source flux sits near the grid edge; note the latent count — and therefore NUTS cost — grows with the padded size, not the effective one (at the defaults 80 + 2·20 = 120, that is 14400 latents for a 6400-pixel source).

knobs.code_doc: Whether to exponentiate the field (ensures positivity).
knobs.curated_html: Exponentiate the Gaussian field so the source intensity is strictly positive (log-normal prior). Disabling allows negative source flux — almost never what you want for a physical galaxy.

knobs.code_doc: Optional spectral priors. ``None`` disables.
knobs.curated_html: Optional NIFTy spectral prior letting the power-spectrum slope vary with scale (an integrated-Wiener-process component on the spectrum). null disables. Enable only when a single power law visibly under-fits both large-scale gradients and small-scale clumps.

knobs.code_doc: GP prior hyperparameters. ``loglogavgslope`` controls smoothness (more negative = smoother); ``fluctuations`` controls amplitude.
knobs.curated_html: Prior on the amplitude of field fluctuations around the mean — how much total power the GP puts into structure. Raise the mean for high-contrast clumpy sources; shrink it if the field starts absorbing noise or lens-light residuals.

knobs.code_doc: Interpolation method for pixel→image-plane mapping.
knobs.curated_html: Interpolation used to map source-grid pixels onto ray-traced image-plane positions. "fast_bilinear" is the JAX-optimised default; other Herculens interpolators trade speed for smoothness of the gradient.

knobs.code_doc: GP prior hyperparameters. ``loglogavgslope`` controls smoothness (more negative = smoother); ``fluctuations`` controls amplitude.
knobs.curated_html: Prior on the average log-log slope of the field's power spectrum — the smoothness dial. More negative mean = smoother fields: −3.0 is a good start for typical hosts; −5 to −6 for very smooth, elliptical-like sources. The std sets how far the data can pull the slope away from the mean.

knobs.code_doc: Log-space mean intensity. ``None`` = estimate from data.
knobs.curated_html: Gaussian-process prior mean intensity, in log-space (the field is exponentiated). null auto-estimates it from the data — rarely needs manual setting; override only when the auto estimate is skewed by contamination inside the arc mask.

knobs.code_doc: Number of pixels per side for the source grid.
knobs.curated_html: Source grid size (N×N pixels). Larger grids resolve more source detail and cost more GPU memory (the field has N² latents before cropping). 80 is fine for most arcs; go to 128–256 for extended or highly structured sources.
warnings: Large grids make geoVI memory-hungry — combine with sampling.nifty.vi.use_multi_gpu=true and a fixed n_samples_per_iteration (the adaptive schedule can OOM).

knobs.code_doc: GP prior hyperparameters. ``loglogavgslope`` controls smoothness (more negative = smoother); ``fluctuations`` controls amplitude.
knobs.curated_html: Prior on the field's global offset amplitude — the (mean, std) of the offset's standard deviation in the NIFTy correlated-field model. The tiny default std essentially pins it; loosen only if the overall source normalisation fights the amplitude latents.

knobs.code_doc: Positive scale factor on the adaptive source-plane grid extent derived from the ray-shot arc mask. 1.0 = full footprint (legacy). Use < 1 when the source is compact compared to the mask footprint, so the CF pixels concentrate on the source instead of empty sky.
knobs.curated_html: Shrink factor on the adaptive source-plane grid extent derived from the ray-shot arc mask. 1.0 keeps the full footprint (legacy behaviour). Use < 1 when the source is compact compared to the mask footprint, so the correlated-field pixels concentrate on the source instead of empty sky — effectively raising the source-plane resolution for free.
warnings: Too small a scale crops real source flux; check the source-plane panel of the model summary after changing it.
