knobs.curated_html: Fraction of steps spent linearly ramping the learning rate from zero — protects against violent early updates from a bad initialisation.

Adam steps PER LEVEL of the annealing ladder (with anneal.lbfgs_maxiter, default 400, as the L-BFGS counterpart). The per-level budget is deliberately small — the ladder's power is the warm-started sequence, not any single level. adam.steps/lbfgs.maxiter are ignored while annealing is on.

L-BFGS iteration cap PER LEVEL of the annealing ladder — the counterpart of anneal.adam_steps. The per-level budget is deliberately small; the ladder's power is the warm-started sequence, not any single level.

knobs.code_doc: Start noise-inflation level of the `"continuous"` anneal mode (default 16): the likelihood noise is multiplied by this factor at the start and decays exponentially to `level_lo`. Needs level_hi > level_lo ≥ 1. Unused by the `"discrete"` ladder.
Final noise level of the continuous anneal (default 1 = the real noise).

NOISE-CONTINUATION ("annealing") for Phase 1. Each start is optimised at noise_map * level, warm-starting the next level, ending at the TRUE noise (1.0 appended if missing). Inflating sigma by L tempers the imaging likelihood to the power 1/L^2 while priors stay untempered, which smooths away shallow local minima that trap flat multistart (graduated non-convexity / continuation — deterministic, NOT simulated annealing). None/[] = historical single-level behaviour. Deeper schedules (e.g. [16,8,4,2,1]) typically help; Phase-2 refinement still runs afterwards at true noise with the standard refinement budgets.
knobs.curated_html:
Noise-continuation ("annealing") Phase 1. When set, every start is optimised at noise_map × level, each level warm-starting the next, ending at the TRUE noise (a final 1.0 is appended if missing) — so the ranked losses are always the real objective. Inflating σ by L tempers the imaging likelihood to the power 1/L² while the priors stay untempered: the smoothed early levels wash out the shallow local minima plain multistart lands in (graduated non-convexity / continuation — deterministic, NOT simulated annealing).

Benchmarks on real quad-lens data: χ²_red 1.07 vs 1.94 from IDENTICAL starts; 6 annealed starts beat the 30+5 flat recipe at ~21% less compute; the flat baseline's best fit had collapsed the source to a delta function and left the Einstein ring unmodelled. Phase-2 refinement runs unchanged afterwards, at true noise.

knobs.code_doc: ANNEAL MODE (2026-08-25). "discrete"   — the ladder above: a fixed noise level per rung. "continuous" — the level decays exponentially from ``anneal_level_hi`` to ``anneal_level_lo`` across ``anneal_segments`` segments.  The level is a TRACED argument, so the whole schedule compiles once instead of once per rung. "off"        — no annealing (equivalent to anneal_levels=None). None resolves to "discrete" when levels are set, "off" otherwise, so existing configs keep their behaviour exactly. DEFAULT-ON (2026-08-27).  Validated on HE0435: 26,212 s -> 4,072 s at chi2_red 3.853 vs the flat-recipe reference 3.850.  Opt out with ``anneal: {mode: "off"}``.  NOTE the dataclass default used to be None -> "off"; a config that never mentions annealing therefore CHANGES behaviour on upgrade (faster, equal-or-better chi2, different numbers).

RAMP the per-rung/segment budget by (index + 1) / n, floored at 50 Adam steps: cheap while the pool is wide and the objective heavily tempered, full budget once the ranking decides.  Measured (pool 32, seed 7, identical otherwise): ramp on -> chi2_red 3.83 in 59360 gradients; ramp off -> 8.04 in 106400.  79% MORE compute, and it fails.  NOTE: ramping applies cleanly to "discrete" mode only.  In "continuous" mode each segment's temperature range is scaled by the same factor so d(log level)/step stays constant -- but that is NOT sufficient: ramped continuous runs still fail (chi2_red 6.1-7.8; 8.5-16.7 without the coupling).  A continuous segment must both CONVERGE and TRACK a moving minimum, so it has a minimum viable step count that ramping violates; a discrete rung only has to converge at a fixed temperature.  Leave ramp off when mode == "continuous". Stays None: __post_init__ resolves it MODE-AWARE (True for discrete, False for continuous -- a ramped continuous segment violates the 300-step floor and fails).
Number of segments of the continuous anneal schedule (default 5). The level is a traced argument, so the whole schedule compiles once instead of once per rung.

How Phase-1/2 starts are executed. "auto"        — pmap across devices when there is more than one (that parallelism is real), otherwise SEQUENTIAL. "vmap"        — the historical chunked path; keep for reproducing pre-2026-08-25 runs. "sequential" / "distributed" — force one. Measured on a 219x219 frame with a 447x447 supersampled PSF: a gradient costs 62 ms at vmap width 1 and 61 ms per start at width 8, so one start already saturates the device and batching buys nothing.  It is worse than neutral: under vmap jaxopt's L-BFGS runs a BATCHED while_loop, so a converged start keeps iterating until its slowest chunk-mate finishes.

SUCCESSIVE HALVING over Phase 1: starts alive at each rung/segment. ``[32, 16, 8, 4, 2]`` screens 32 basins for less total compute than the flat recipe spends on 10, because only survivors pay full budget. None = no pruning (every start walks the whole ladder). Must have one entry per rung (discrete) or segment (continuous), and be non-increasing.

L-BFGS implementation. "optax" (default) uses a zoom line search with Wolfe conditions and terminates on the gradient norm; "jaxopt" runs a fixed maxiter regardless of progress and is unmaintained.  Measured on identical schedules (b=0 HE0435, pool 32): optax loss 170720 in 2597 s, jaxopt 171378 in 3153 s -- better and ~18%% faster.  Keep "jaxopt" to reproduce pre-2026-08-25 runs.

knobs.curated_html: Reduced-χ² threshold that triggers a retry (when retries are enabled). Also a useful sanity number: a converged fit far above it usually means a data/config problem (wrong pixel scale, missing mask, bad PSF), not bad luck.

knobs.curated_html: Total optimisation attempts: if the best reduced χ² exceeds chi2_red_threshold, the multistart is retried with fresh randomness, up to this many total attempts. 2–3 enables automatic retries.

knobs.curated_html: Save the top-N parameter sets from each phase to disk — useful for diagnosing multimodality and for warm-starting later runs.

knobs.code_doc: Number of random multistart initialisations. ``None`` (default) resolves by optimizer mode: 10 when an anneal ladder is set (annealing removes the multistart lottery — nearly every start flows into the same basin, so redundancy beyond ~10 is wasted compute), 50 for flat multistart (which needs the lottery). Phase-1 random starts.
knobs.curated_html: Number of Phase-1 random starts. The worked example uses 10 together with the annealing ladder, which removes much of the multistart lottery. Flat multistart runs generally benefit from at least 50; use 100–200 for production runs on lenses with strong degeneracies.

knobs.code_doc: Phase 1 vmap chunk fallback ladder for multi-start GD (largest tried first). Hardware-dependent: [10, 5, 1] is fastest on >=40GB cards; the conservative default [5, 2, 1] is required on 24GB cards with 199^2 frames (a failed chunk-10 attempt fragments the pool; anomaly 003).
knobs.curated_html: vmap chunk fallback ladder for multi-start GD — how many starts are batched through one vmapped evaluation, largest tried first with OOM fallback down the ladder. Hardware-dependent: [10, 5, 1] is fastest on ≥ 40 GB cards; the conservative default is required on 24 GB cards with ~200² frames.
warnings: A failed large-chunk attempt fragments the GPU memory pool (anomaly 003) — on smaller cards, don't lead with an optimistic chunk size.

knobs.code_doc: Maximum shapelet order of the stage-1 source.
knobs.curated_html: Maximum Shapelet order. The number of basis functions grows as (n_max+1)(n_max+2)/2 — n_max=16 gives 153 components. Higher orders resolve finer source structure but add latents and can start fitting noise or absorbing PSF residuals. Unused unless source_type="shapelets" or the staged CF flow (whose stage 1 is a Shapelets fit).

knobs.code_doc: Source model of the GD stage: shapelets | sersic | double-sersic | corr_field. 'shapelets' is required for the staged CorrField pipeline.
knobs.curated_html: Source representation used during the stage-1 multi-start gradient descent. "shapelets" (Sersic + shapelet basis, size n_max) is the production default — smooth, analytic and fast to optimise from random starts. "sersic" drops the shapelets. "corr_field" runs GD directly on a pixelated correlated-field source (no staged flow; expensive and non-convex — the staged shapelets → CF path exists precisely because this is hard).
